# Security and Supply-Chain Checklist: PB Installer for Linux

**Purpose**: Check that the security and supply-chain requirements of a program that downloads from the network and writes to a removable drive are complete, clear, consistent and measurable before planning.
**Created**: 2026-10-25
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Scope**: requirements only (spec.md; constitution Principles III, IV, V and VI; contracts `catalog-format.md` and `package-manifest.md`; `docs/review-checks.md`). Depth: formal pre-plan gate. Audience: author and reviewer. There is no plan.md yet, so items that need a design decision are marked `[Gap]`. Install safety (staging, journal, recovery, backups, removal) is covered separately in [install-safety.md](install-safety.md) and is not repeated here.

## Catalog Authenticity and Rollback Protection

- [ ] CHK001 Is it stated that nothing from the catalog is interpreted, shown or acted on before its signature has verified, and that this holds for every front end and every action (list, install, update, adopt)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006, Constitution §III]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the first run defined, when no last accepted serial is on record yet (accept any verified catalog, or something stricter), and is the choice stated as a deliberate trust decision? [Gap, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK003 Is behavior defined when the record of the last accepted serial is missing, damaged or unreadable (for example deleted by the user), so that losing the file cannot be used to switch rollback protection off without notice? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-007, §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK004 Is it specified where that record lives on the computer, who can write to it, and what it contains besides the serial (it must hold nothing that identifies the user)? [Gap, Spec §Clarifications, §FR-007, §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK005 Is the case of an equal serial with different catalog bytes addressed, rather than only "an equal serial is accepted as unchanged"? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases "older serial"]
- [ ] CHK006 Is a freshness requirement stated or deliberately excluded: an old, genuinely signed catalog with a serial at or above the last accepted one could keep offering a version that has since been withdrawn, so must the user be told how old the catalog is? [Gap, Spec §FR-007, §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK007 Is the handling of a trusted key that has been compromised or retired defined for installers already in users' hands, given that there is no update check of the installer itself? [Gap, Spec §Assumptions, Out of Scope]
- [ ] CHK008 Is the rule that the signature is checked against every key in the built-in list, and passes if any one verifies, written so that "short list, for rotation" has a stated upper size and a stated owner of changes to it? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006]

## Transport Security

- [ ] CHK009 Does the certificate-verification requirement cover every download (catalog, signature and package), or only the catalog and its signature as FR-006 reads? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-006, §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK010 Are redirects addressed (HTTPS only, a maximum number, any host allowed, as the package host redirects to other hosts), and is a redirect to plain HTTP an explicit failure with a rule id? [Coverage, Spec §FR-006, docs/contracts/catalog-format.md]
- [ ] CHK011 Is the source of trust anchors for certificates specified (system store, a bundled list, or both), as Principle III requires, for a self-contained program that cannot rely on what is installed? [Gap, Constitution §III, Spec §FR-033]
- [ ] CHK012 Is it stated that no setting, option, environment variable or file can weaken or switch off certificate or host-name checks, or point the program at another catalog address or trust root, outside of a test-only mechanism that is itself defined? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006, Constitution §III]
- [ ] CHK013 Do the requirements agree on how tests supply "a test copy of the catalog" (User Story 1) while "the catalog is fetched from its one stable address" (FR-006), without a production code path that skips verification? [Conflict, Spec §US1 Independent Test, §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK014 Are size bounds required for each download (catalog, signature, package), stopping the transfer at the limit and at the signed size rather than after the whole file has arrived? [Coverage, Spec §FR-008, docs/contracts/catalog-format.md]
- [ ] CHK015 Are the different transport failures (host unreachable, certificate invalid or expired, wrong host name, interception by a proxy, wrong system clock) distinguished in the messages, none of them suggesting to turn verification off? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases "No network", §FR-030]

## Package Integrity and Manifest Match

- [ ] CHK016 Is the order of checks fixed in the requirements (size limit, SHA-256 against the signed entry, then ZIP and manifest rules, then cross-checks), so that nothing from the package is parsed before its hash has matched? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK017 Is it required that the bytes written to the reader are exactly the bytes that were verified (verified once, kept, and not downloaded or read again from a place that could change in between)? [Gap, Spec §FR-008, §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK018 Does FR-008 name which cross-checks apply to a catalog install and which to a local file, and are `E-ENT-13`, `E-ENT-14`, `E-ENT-15` and `E-ENT-17` each tied to a defined failure message? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK019 Is the requirement that the manifest's `id`, `version`, minimum firmware, target device and menu entry id equal the signed entry stated as an install gate in this feature, not only as a property of the shared check? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008, docs/contracts/package-manifest.md]
- [ ] CHK020 Are the rule ids that can appear in a message limited to ones the contract defines, and is a failing check for a rule the program does not know (a newer contract) specified as "refuse, needs updating"? [Consistency, Spec §FR-030, §Edge Cases "newer major schema"]

## Hostile Package Content and Names

- [ ] CHK021 Are path traversal (`..`), absolute paths, hidden names, over-long names and characters outside the allowed set all named as refused, each tied to a rule id the user sees? [Coverage, Spec §FR-008, §US2 scenario 4]
- [ ] CHK022 Is the complete list of places a package may cause a write stated in one place (the `applications/` tree, the menu entry, the installer's own folder) and is anything else defined as refused, including the app's data folder, which the package must never fill? [Completeness, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-017, §FR-034]
- [ ] CHK023 Are symbolic links inside the package refused, and are links, or a folder replaced by a link, that already exist in the target tree (for a folder chosen by hand) addressed so that a write cannot leave the reader's root? [Gap, Spec §US2 scenario 4, §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK024 Is the case-insensitive collision rule stated for names that differ only by letter case between a package file and a file already on the reader (not only inside the package), with the outcome defined? [Gap, Spec §Assumptions "FAT-type volume", §FR-017]
- [ ] CHK025 Is it defined what happens when a package file path is already owned by another installed app's install record, so that one app cannot take over or overwrite another app's files? [Gap, Spec §FR-016, §FR-017]
- [ ] CHK026 Are the package limits (compressed and uncompressed size, entry count, compression ratio) required to hold for packages from every source, and is the check required to run before anything is written or staged? [Coverage, Spec §FR-008, §FR-025]
- [ ] CHK027 Is it stated that nothing is extracted to a temporary location outside the reader's staging area, including the computer's temporary folder, before the checks have passed? [Gap, Spec §FR-008, §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK028 Are file names and package text shown to the user (manifest `name`, menu `title`, file names, descriptions) required to be shown as plain text, with control characters and terminal escape sequences neutralised in command-line output, the log and the graphical assistant? [Gap, Spec §FR-030, §FR-031]

## Claims on Menu Entries, Data Folders and Reserved Names

- [ ] CHK029 Is the refusal of a package whose menu entry id is already used by another app in the desktop configuration written for every holder: installed by this program, installed by hand, and a vendor entry the program did not create? [Coverage, Spec §FR-026, §FR-017]
- [ ] CHK030 Is the same rule written for the data folder, including a `system/<name>` folder that already exists on the reader and belongs to no installed app, so that a package cannot adopt someone else's folder? [Gap, Spec §FR-026]
- [ ] CHK031 Are reserved data folder names stated as a requirement on the installer (checked on the reader as well as in the package), with the source of the list, how it grows, and the fact that it was verified on one model and firmware? [Gap, Spec §FR-008, docs/security-review.md "Reserved data folder names"]
- [ ] CHK032 Is `system/pbstore` required to be refused as a claim by a package, even though it is not on the contract's reserved list and the contract is out of scope for change? [Consistency, Spec §FR-034, §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK033 Is the comparison of menu entry ids and data folder names defined with the volume's case rules (two ids or folders differing only by letter case count as the same claim)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-026, §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK034 Is it addressed that a package's menu title or name could imitate a vendor's or another app's, and is the plan required to show the origin of each app so that the constitution's rule not to imply endorsement by PocketBook holds? [Gap, Constitution §VIII, Spec §FR-011, §FR-025]

## Local ZIP Files as Untrusted Input

- [ ] CHK035 Is a local ZIP stated to receive the same hostile-input checks as a downloaded package, with the exact list of what cannot be checked (no signed entry, so no hash or entry cross-check) written out instead of "all package checks run"? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-025, §US6]
- [ ] CHK036 Is it defined what happens when a local ZIP's app id, menu entry id or data folder matches an app of the catalog that is not installed (and whether this can pre-empt a later catalog install)? [Gap, Spec §US6 scenario 2, §FR-026]
- [ ] CHK037 Is the kind of file accepted as a local ZIP specified (a regular file only; not a device, pipe or link to another place), and is a file that changes while it is being read handled? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §US6]
- [ ] CHK038 Is the "not from the catalog, not signed by the maintainer" label required to appear at confirmation time in a way the user cannot miss (for example an explicit extra confirmation), rather than only as a marking? [Clarity, Spec §FR-025, §US6 scenario 1]
- [ ] CHK039 Is it stated that a local ZIP can never lead the program to change its trusted keys, the last accepted serial or its catalog state? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-007, §FR-025]

## Logs, Messages and Privacy

- [ ] CHK040 Is "personal data" defined for logs and messages beyond the four listed examples, including the mount path of the reader (which usually contains the user name), the volume label, the path of a local ZIP, and the computer's host name? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-031, §Edge Cases "Several readers"]
- [ ] CHK041 Do the requirements agree between FR-031 (no personal data in logs) and the places where the program must name drives and files to the user (the list of several readers, plans, local ZIP paths), by saying what may be shown on screen versus what may be written to the log? [Conflict, Spec §FR-031, §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK042 Is "secret" defined for a program that holds no signing key (for example credentials inside a proxy address or a download address), so that "no secrets" is a testable rule and not an empty one? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-031, §SC-010]
- [ ] CHK043 Is it specified where the log is kept (on the computer, never on the reader), who can read it, how long it is kept, and whether it can be turned off? [Gap, Spec §FR-031]
- [ ] CHK044 Are the contents of the network requests specified (no identifier, no machine or user details beyond what an HTTPS request inevitably carries, including the program's name and version in the request), consistent with "no telemetry, no identifier"? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010, Constitution §V]
- [ ] CHK045 Is it stated that the program never needs, asks for or advises elevated rights, and that it never writes outside the reader's folder, its own state and its log location on the computer? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases "without rights to write"]
- [ ] CHK046 Are the links from the catalog (source, changelog, icon) specified as shown but not opened or fetched without a user action, and as limited to HTTPS? [Gap, Spec §FR-010, docs/contracts/catalog-format.md]

## The Published Download and Its Checksum

- [ ] CHK047 Is the way a user checks a download against the published SHA-256 (the command, and where the sums are published) required as part of the release, and is it stated honestly that a checksum from the same place as the download shows integrity, not authenticity? [Clarity, Spec §FR-033, Constitution §Security]
- [ ] CHK048 Is it decided whether the `SHA256SUMS` file is signed with the maintainer key, and does the spec say what a user can rely on if it is not? [Gap, Spec §FR-033]
- [ ] CHK049 Are requirements for the build's provenance stated (built from a tagged release in CI, dependencies pinned and reviewed, third-party licenses listed), or deliberately left to the plan? [Traceability, Gap, Constitution §Security & Data Handling, Spec §FR-033]
- [ ] CHK050 Is the claim "no runtime to install" consistent with the trust anchors, certificate bundle and key list that must be inside the download (CHK011), and is the set of things that ship inside it written down? [Consistency, Spec §FR-033, §FR-006]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK051 Does the success criteria list a hostile-package set (traversal, absolute path, link, case collision, reserved name, claimed entry, oversize, ratio bomb) with 100% refusal and an unchanged reader, instead of the general "contract violation" case in SC-003? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK052 Can SC-010 ("no user name, home path, e-mail address, device serial number or secret") be checked objectively, given the open definitions in CHK040 and CHK042? [Measurability, Spec §SC-010]
- [ ] CHK053 Is each of the signature, rollback, certificate, hash and manifest checks mapped to at least one acceptance scenario that a reviewer can trace? [Traceability, Spec §US1, §FR-006..FR-008]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Most likely to need a spec edit before planning: CHK009 (which downloads are covered by certificate checks), CHK013 and CHK012 (test access to the catalog versus the one stable address), CHK032 (`pbstore` is not on the contract's reserved list), CHK030 and CHK036 (claims by a package on existing folders and on catalog apps), CHK041 and CHK040 (what may be logged versus shown), CHK048 (signing the checksums)
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference; numbering starts again at CHK001 in each checklist file
